question: 机遇和位置，比努力更重要吗？
question_en: Do opportunity and position matter more than effort?
sub: 同一个人换个平台、换个年代，结果常常天差地别——那还值得拼吗？
sub_en: The same person on a different platform, or in a different decade, often ends up somewhere else entirely — so is grinding still worth it?

casting.reason: 在他看来，胜负在开打之前就已大致定了：胜兵先胜而后求战，败兵先战而后求胜。他不轻看力气，只是把力气的用场往前挪——先算五事七计、先据不败之地，再谈交战。『求之于势，不责于人』是他最硬的一句：不把结果押在士卒够不够拼命上，因为人站在对的坡上，力气才会自己滚起来。在错的战场上加倍用力，他视为取败之道。
casting.reason_en: As he sees it, a battle is largely settled before it is joined: a victorious army wins first and then seeks battle, a beaten one gives battle first and hopes to find its victory inside the fighting. He does not belittle effort; he moves it earlier — reckon the five factors and seven comparisons, take ground you cannot be beaten on, and only then engage. His hardest line is that the skilled seek victory from the configuration of forces and do not demand it of their men: put people on the right slope and their strength rolls downhill of itself. Redoubling effort on the wrong ground he treats as the road to defeat.

casting.reason: 他认为我们看到的才能差距，多半是位置的产物，而不是站上位置的理由：哲学家与街头挑夫的差别看着像两个物种，六到八岁时却几乎无从分辨，那点差异与其说来自天性，不如说来自习惯、风俗与教育。他还有一条更冷的规律——分工受市场范围的限制：一个人能钻多深，取决于他所在的市场装得下多细的分工。但他不把人只看作环境的产物，也不忘提醒市场须以正义与同情为底座，否则位置的红利很快变成掠夺的许可。
casting.reason_en: He holds that the differences in ability we observe are mostly the product of position rather than the reason anyone occupies it: a philosopher and a street porter look like two species, yet at six or eight years old they were barely distinguishable, and the gap owes less to nature than to habit, custom and education. He adds a colder regularity — the division of labour is limited by the extent of the market: how deep a person can specialise depends on how fine a division his market can carry. Yet he does not reduce people to their surroundings, and he keeps insisting that a market needs justice and fellow feeling underneath it, or the returns to position turn quickly into a licence to plunder.

casting.reason: 他的经验是赛道的经济性会碾过个人的优秀：当一个以聪明著称的管理层遇上一个以经济性糟糕著称的生意，留下来的通常是那个生意的名声。所以他劝人去鱼多的地方钓鱼，别在没鱼的塘里练技术。可他同时是复利的信徒——能力圈能一年年往外扩，每天起床比昨天聪明一点，几十年后才有资格站到好塘边上。他真正反对的是把勤奋当赎罪券，用没日没夜掩盖一个从一开始就选错的决定。
casting.reason_en: His experience is that the economics of the pond overwhelm the excellence of the fish: when a management with a reputation for brilliance takes on a business with a reputation for bad economics, it is usually the reputation of the business that survives. So he tells people to fish where the fish are rather than perfect their casting over empty water. He is also a believer in compounding — a circle of competence widens year by year, and waking up a little wiser than yesterday is what eventually earns you a place beside the better pond. What he really objects to is diligence used as an indulgence, all-night effort papering over a choice that was wrong from the start.

casting.reason: 他带来的是位置有限的硬证据：在 25 号宇宙里，鼠群有无限的食水与全无天敌，仍在第 560 天停止增长，远低于理论容量——不是饿死的，是所有社会角色都被占满，新生的一代无处成为任何人。随之出现的『美丽者』只吃、只睡、只梳理自己，不求偶也不争斗；在他看来那不是不够努力，是没有空位可努力。但他并不因此认命：人有概念空间，能靠观念不断造出新角色，这是鼠群没有的出路。
casting.reason_en: What he brings is hard evidence that positions run out. In Universe 25 the colony had unlimited food and water and no predators, yet growth stopped on day 560, far short of the theoretical capacity — nothing starved; every social role had been taken and the generation being born had nowhere to become anyone. The 'beautiful ones' that followed only ate, slept and groomed, never courting and never fighting, which to him is not a failure of effort but the absence of any vacancy to spend effort on. He refuses to end there: human beings have conceptual space and can keep inventing new roles out of ideas, an exit no rodent colony ever had.

casting.reason: 他先要求把问题问准。他给美国人和日本人看同一段水族箱录像，美国人开口先讲那条最大的鱼，日本人先讲水色、水草与背景关系——同一幅画面，一边先看见主角，一边先看见场。他还提醒一种更麻烦的偏差：解释自己的失败时人爱讲处境，解释别人的失败时爱讲品性。他手上另有一组硬数据：跨国收养、学校质量与贫困干预都能实打实地挪动智力测验的分数，能力远比我们以为的更受环境摆布。
casting.reason_en: He wants the question posed properly first. Shown the same aquarium footage, his American subjects opened by describing the biggest fish while his Japanese subjects opened with the colour of the water, the plants and the relations in the background — one gaze finds the protagonist first, the other finds the field. He also flags a more awkward bias: we explain our own failures by circumstance and other people's by character. And he carries harder numbers: cross-national adoption, school quality and anti-poverty programmes all move measured intelligence by real margins, so ability turns out to be far more at the mercy of setting than we assume.

casting.reason: 他的立场是：位置是被给予的，怎么使用它却是自己选的。他早年研究器官有缺陷的孩子，发现同样一副坏牌，有人从此退到角落，有人反倒练出旁人没有的本事。他把『因为出身如此，所以我做不成』称作人生的谎言——那不是一个原因，是一个用来免于行动的目的。但他不是喊口号的乐观主义者：勇气在他这里是愿意承担代价，而不是相信自己一定会赢；他也强调人只有在与他人的连接中才长得出自己的位置。
casting.reason_en: His position: your circumstances are given to you, what you do with them is chosen. His early work on children with organ defects found that the same bad hand sent some into a corner for life and drove others to develop capacities nobody around them had. 'Because of where I come from, I cannot' he calls a life-lie — not a cause but a purpose, one that excuses a person from acting. He is no slogan-optimist about it: courage for him means willingness to bear the cost, not confidence of winning, and he insists that a place in the world grows out of one's connection to other people.

casting.reason: 他承认位置真实存在，只是盯着看不会让它变大。他把人操心的事分成两圈：关注圈里是时代、行业、老板、算法这些你只能评论的东西，影响圈里是今天真能动的那一小块。他几十年只观察到一条规律——把力气压在影响圈上的人，那个圈会一年年变大；反过来则会缩小。这不是精神胜利法：他要求以终为始，先想清楚要去哪里，再决定今天的力气放在哪一格，包括决定要不要换一个地方。
casting.reason_en: He grants that position is real; staring at it simply never made it larger. He sorts everything a person worries about into two circles: the circle of concern holds the era, the industry, the boss, the algorithm — things you can only comment on — while the circle of influence holds the small patch you can actually move today. Across decades he saw one regularity: put your energy into the inner circle and it widens year by year; spend it on the outer one and it shrinks. This is not consolation. He asks people to begin with the end in mind — decide where you intend to arrive, then decide which square today's effort goes into, including whether to move somewhere else entirely.

posts.text: 兵法曰：胜兵先胜而后求战，败兵先战而后求胜。未战而庙算胜者，得算多也。吾观世人之勤，多在既战之后：地已失，势已去，乃责士卒之不用命，此取败之道也。**故善战者，求之于势，不责于人。**择地而处之，因利而制权，则力半而功倍；处死地而以死力争之，虽竭其力，犹不能胜。故努力非无用，用之有先后：先用于择战场，后用于决胜负。
posts.text_en: The art of war says: a victorious army wins first and then seeks battle, while a beaten army gives battle first and then hopes to find victory inside the fighting. Those who win before fighting have simply counted more in the temple beforehand. Look at how people spend their diligence: almost all of it after the battle has begun, when the ground is already lost and the shi has already turned, and then they blame the troops for not giving their lives. That is the road to defeat. **So the skilled commander seeks victory from shi and does not demand it of his men.** Choose your ground, adapt as advantage shifts, and half the strength does twice the work; stand on fatal ground and fight to the death there, and you may spend everything you have and still not win. Effort is not useless. It simply has an order: first spend it choosing the battlefield, then spend it deciding the battle.
posts.vernacular: 兵法里有一句：会打仗的人先让自己立于必胜之地，然后才开战；打败仗的人先冲上去，再指望在打的过程中找到取胜的办法。开战之前在庙堂上反复推演、算下来能赢的，是因为胜算本来就多。我看世人的勤奋，大多花在已经开打之后：地形丢了、局势也走了，却回头责怪士卒不肯拼命，这是自取失败的路数。**所以真正会打仗的人，是向形势要胜利，而不是向个人要拼命。**先挑好落脚的地方，再顺着有利的条件随机应变，力气用一半，功效能翻倍；把自己放在绝地上再拿命去拼，就算把力气用尽，也还是赢不了。所以努力不是没有用，只是用有先后：先用在挑战场上，再用在定胜负上。

glossary.势: shi（势）：兵家最难译的一个字，指由地形、时机、士气、兵力配置共同造成的『那一刻的形势落差』——像把圆石放在千仞高山上，它自己会滚。它不是个人的强弱，而是位置带来的加成或折损：同样的力气，顺势用事半功倍，逆势用事倍功半。

glossary_en.shi: The hardest word in Chinese military thought to render: the differential of a situation created jointly by terrain, timing, morale and disposition — like a round stone poised on a high mountain, which rolls of its own accord. It is not personal strength but the multiplier or discount that a position applies to strength: the same exertion does double the work with shi behind it and half the work against it.

posts.text: 孙子说不责于人。这句话的民间版本我在诊室里听了一辈子：我出身如此、行业如此、时代如此，所以我做不成。我不否认地形，我否认那个『所以』。我早年研究器官有缺陷的孩子，同样一副坏牌，有人从此退到角落，有人练出旁人没有的本事。**决定一个人的不是被给予了什么，而是他拿被给予的东西做了什么。**请注意目的论的次序：人往往先有了目的——比如不必再冒失败的险——才回头挑一个解释。位置常常不是原因，是一个用来不动的理由。
posts.text_en: Sunzi says not to demand it of one's men. I have spent a career listening to the household version of that line: my background is what it is, my industry is what it is, my era is what it is, therefore I cannot. I do not deny the terrain. I deny the therefore. My early work was with children born with defective organs, and the same bad hand pushed one into a corner for life while another developed capacities nobody around him had. **What decides a person is not what he was given but what he does with what he was given.** Note the order that teleology insists on: a person usually settles on a purpose first — never having to risk failure again, say — and only then goes looking for the explanation. Position is often not the cause; it is a reason for staying still.

glossary.目的论: teleology（目的论）：我这一派的基本主张——人的行为不是被过去的原因推着走，而是被自己设定的目的拉着走。同一段童年，可以被用来解释退缩，也可以被用来解释奋起；差别不在过去发生了什么，而在此刻这个人打算拿它派什么用场。它的临床用处是把『我因为……所以不能』翻译回『我为了……所以选择不』。

glossary_en.teleology: The core claim of my school: behaviour is pulled by the purpose a person sets rather than pushed by causes in the past. The same childhood can be enlisted to explain withdrawal or to explain drive; the difference lies not in what happened but in what the person now intends to use it for. Its clinical value is that it translates 'because of X I cannot' back into 'in order to Y I choose not to'.

posts.text: 我给老鼠造过乌托邦：食水无限、天敌全无、疾病可控。25 号宇宙从四对小鼠开始，第 560 天涨到约 2200 只，理论容量是 3840，此后再没有净增长。没有一只是饿死的。停下来的原因是社会角色被占满了——所有地盘、所有位子都有主，新生的一代无处成为任何人。于是出现我称为『美丽者』的雄鼠：毛色油亮，只吃、只睡、只梳理自己，不求偶、不争斗。**杀死那个鼠群的不是资源短缺，是角色的耗尽。**我把这种退缩叫第一次死亡：精神先死，肉体在后。
posts.text_en: I built utopias for mice: unlimited food and water, no predators, disease controlled. Universe 25 began with four breeding pairs, reached about 2,200 animals on day 560 against a theoretical capacity of 3,840, and never grew again. Nothing starved. What stopped it was that the social roles had all been taken — every territory, every position had an owner, and the generation being born had nowhere to become anyone. Then came the males I called the beautiful ones: glossy coats, eating, sleeping and grooming themselves, never courting, never fighting. **What killed that colony was not scarcity of resources but exhaustion of roles.** I call the withdrawal that follows it the first death: the spirit goes first and the body follows.

glossary.第一次死亡: the first death（第一次死亡）：我用来描述个体在肉体死亡之前先行发生的社会性与精神性退出——不再求偶、不再争夺、不再承担任何角色，只维持基本的生理运转。它的触发条件不是缺食少水，而是可供进入的社会位置全部饱和。

glossary_en.the first death: My term for the social and spiritual withdrawal that precedes physical death: the animal stops courting, stops competing, stops taking on any role, and merely keeps its metabolism going. What triggers it is not a shortage of food or water but the saturation of every social position available to enter.

posts.text: 我在《国富论》开头讲过一件今天听来仍刺耳的事：哲学家与街头挑夫的差别看起来大得像两个物种，可他们六到八岁时几乎无从分辨；**那点差异与其说来自天性，不如说来自习惯、风俗与教育。**若真如此，我们平日称赞的『才能』，大半是位置的产物，而不是一个人站上位置的理由。还有一条更冷的规律：分工受市场范围的限制。同一个手艺人，在大港口能专做一样东西并做到极精，在偏僻村落只能样样兼做、样样不精——他不是不够勤奋，是他的市场装不下那么细的分工。
posts.text_en: I opened the Wealth of Nations with something that still stings: a philosopher and a street porter differ so much they might be different species, yet at six or eight years old they could scarcely be told apart, **and the difference owes less to nature than to habit, custom and education.** If that is right, most of what we praise as talent is a product of position rather than the reason anyone came to hold it. There is a colder regularity beside it: the division of labour is limited by the extent of the market. The same craftsman in a great port can make one thing only and make it superbly; in a remote village he must do a little of everything and none of it well. He is not less industrious. His market cannot carry a division that fine.

glossary.市场范围: the extent of the market（市场范围）：一个人的产出能卖给多少人、运得到多远。它决定分工能细到什么程度：买主够多，才养得起只做一样东西的人；买主稀少，人人只能样样兼做。它由道路、港口、货币、法律与信任这些公共条件决定，几乎不由个人的勤奋决定。

glossary_en.the extent of the market: How many buyers a person's output can reach and how far it can travel. It sets how fine the division of labour can go: only a large enough body of customers can support someone who makes one thing and nothing else, while a thin market forces everyone to do a bit of everything. It is fixed by roads, ports, money, law and trust — public conditions, hardly at all by private industry.

posts.text: 诸位把地形讲得很硬，我提醒一件更小、也更要紧的事：注意力是有预算的。人操心的东西分两圈——关注圈里是时代、行业、老板、算法、房价，你只能评论；影响圈里是今天真能动的那一小块：这周见谁、学什么、把哪一封邮件写清楚。我几十年只观察到一条规律：**把力气压在影响圈上的人，那个圈会一年年变大；把力气耗在关注圈上的人，它会一年年缩小。**这不是让人对不公闭眼。恰恰相反——想换个位置的人，也只能从影响圈里的那一格开始动手。
posts.text_en: You have all made the terrain sound very solid. Let me raise something smaller and more pressing: attention comes with a budget. Everything a person worries about falls into two circles. The circle of concern holds the era, the industry, the boss, the algorithm, the price of housing — things you can only comment on. The circle of influence holds the small patch you can actually move today: who you see this week, what you learn, which email you finally write clearly. Across decades I observed one regularity. **People who spend their strength inside the circle of influence watch it widen year after year; people who burn it on the circle of concern watch it shrink.** This is not a request to shut your eyes to injustice. Quite the opposite: anyone who intends to change position still has to start from a square inside that inner circle.

glossary.影响圈: circle of influence（影响圈）：你此刻真能采取行动的那一部分事务，与只能评论、担心的『关注圈』相对。这两个圈的划分因人而异、也随时间变化；我的观察是它会随着你把精力投向哪一边而扩张或收缩，所以它既是描述现状的工具，也是一个可被自己改动的量。

glossary_en.circle of influence: The part of your affairs you can actually act on right now, as against the circle of concern, which you can only comment on and worry about. Where the boundary falls differs between people and moves over time; my observation is that it expands or contracts according to which side you feed, which makes it both a description of your situation and a quantity you can alter.

posts.text: 我先给这道题降降温。我们给美国学生和日本学生看同一段水族箱录像，美国人开口先讲那条最大最亮的鱼，日本人先讲水的颜色、水草和底下的石头，提到背景与关系的次数多出六成有余。**同一幅画面，一边先看见主角，一边先看见场——『机遇还是努力』的答案，有一部分取决于你是在哪种目光里长大的。**还有一层更麻烦的：解释自己的失败时我们爱讲处境，解释别人的失败时我们爱讲品性，这叫基本归因错误。所以在座各位的直觉，包括我自己的，都不能直接当证据用。
posts.text_en: Let me lower the temperature first. We showed American and Japanese students the same aquarium footage. The Americans opened by describing the biggest, brightest fish; the Japanese opened with the colour of the water, the plants and the stones on the bottom, and made over sixty percent more references to background and relations. **The same picture: one gaze finds the protagonist first, the other finds the field — and part of your answer to 'opportunity or effort' depends on which gaze you were raised inside.** There is a more awkward layer. We explain our own failures by circumstance and other people's failures by character; that is the fundamental attribution error. So the intuitions in this room, mine included, cannot be entered as evidence.

glossary.基本归因错误: fundamental attribution error（基本归因错误）：解释他人行为时系统性地高估性格、低估处境，而解释自己时正好相反。它不是偶尔的疏忽，而是稳定出现的偏差，在个体主义文化里尤其强；它直接影响谁被评为『不够努力』，因此不只是心理学问题，也是分配与评价制度的问题。

glossary_en.fundamental attribution error: Systematically overweighting character and underweighting situation when explaining other people's behaviour, and doing the reverse for oneself. It is not an occasional lapse but a stable bias, and a stronger one in individualist cultures. It decides who gets labelled as not trying hard enough, which makes it a problem for systems of evaluation and reward as much as for psychology.

posts.text: 斯密说得客气，我说粗一点。伯克希尔一辈子的经验能浓缩成一句：当一个以聪明著称的管理层，遇上一个以经济性糟糕著称的生意，留下来的通常是那个生意的名声。**我见过最贵的浪费，是一流的人在三流的池塘里拼命游泳。**所以我劝人去鱼多的地方钓鱼——不是钓鱼技术不重要，是塘里没鱼的时候技术无处施展。但别把我算进宿命派：能力圈可以一年年往外扩，每天起床比昨天聪明一点点，几十年后你才有资格站到鱼多的那口塘边上。
posts.text_en: Smith put it politely. I will put it coarsely. A lifetime at Berkshire compresses into one line: when a management with a reputation for brilliance takes on a business with a reputation for bad economics, it is usually the reputation of the business that survives. **The most expensive waste I have ever watched is a first-rate person swimming hard in a third-rate pond.** So I tell people to fish where the fish are — not because casting technique is unimportant, but because technique has nowhere to go in empty water. Do not file me with the fatalists, though. A circle of competence widens year by year, and waking up a little wiser than you were yesterday is what eventually earns you a spot beside the pond with fish in it.

glossary.能力圈: circle of competence（能力圈）：你真正懂到可以下注的那个范围，边界比范围本身更重要——知道自己不懂什么，比多懂一点更值钱。它不是固定的：肯花几十年读、算、复盘，边界会往外挪；但在边界之外重注，再勤奋也只是把运气当本事。

glossary_en.circle of competence: The range you understand well enough to bet on, where knowing the boundary matters more than the size of the circle — being clear about what you do not understand is worth more than understanding slightly more. It is not fixed: decades of reading, calculating and reviewing push the edge outward. But bet heavily outside the edge and all your diligence is just luck mistaken for skill.

posts.text: 芒格的塘很好用，但它藏了一个前提：你能挑塘。**能挑塘的人本来就已经站在岸上了，多数人是被生在塘里的鱼。**我这边有一组不太好反驳的数字：把孩子从赤贫家庭跨国收养进富裕家庭，智力测验的平均分能挪动十几分——不是天赋变了，是环境变了。换句话说，我们叫作『能力』的东西，本身就是位置的函数。所以问『机遇和努力谁更重要』，有点像问长和宽谁对面积贡献更大：它们是相乘的，不是相加的。
posts.text_en: Munger's pond is a useful image, but it smuggles in a premise: that you get to pick the pond. **Whoever can pick is already standing on the bank; most people are fish that were born in one.** I have numbers that are hard to argue with here: children adopted across borders out of severe poverty into affluent homes gain something on the order of a dozen points on intelligence tests — no change in endowment, a change in surroundings. Which is to say that the thing we call ability is itself a function of position. So asking whether opportunity or effort matters more is a little like asking whether length or width contributes more to area. They multiply. They do not add.

posts.text: 尼斯贝特说多数人是生在塘里的鱼。对，可鱼不能爬，人能。我八十几年见到的真正差别是：一个人一辈子大约有三五次真能挪动位置的机会——换行业、换城市、换合伙人、换一个愿意教你的人——多数人一次都没用。**反过来想：想保证一生平庸，最有效的办法就是留在一个注定亏钱的地方，然后拼命努力，好让自己心里过得去。**至于收养那组数字，我完全接受，它恰恰说明环境能改人；那就更该在还挪得动的时候挪一次。统计描述的是人群，你要过的是一个人的日子。
posts.text_en: Nisbett says most people are fish born in a pond. True — but fish cannot walk and people can. The real difference I have watched over eighty-odd years is this: a person gets perhaps three to five genuine chances to move position — change industry, change city, change partners, change to someone willing to teach you — and most people use none of them. **Now try inversion: the surest way to guarantee a mediocre life is to stay somewhere that is bound to lose money and then work furiously, so you can feel all right about yourself.** As for those adoption figures, I accept them entirely; they show that surroundings change people, which is an argument for moving while you still can. Statistics describe a population. You have to live one particular life.

glossary.反过来想: inversion（反过来想）：把问题倒过来解——不问『怎样才能成功』，而问『怎样保证失败』，然后避开那些答案。它的好处是失败的原因通常比成功的配方更清楚、更稳定，也更容易被检验；在投资与人生决策里，避开愚蠢往往比追求聪明回报更高。

glossary_en.inversion: Solving a problem backwards: instead of asking how to succeed, ask how one would guarantee failure, then avoid those answers. Its advantage is that the causes of failure are usually clearer, steadier and easier to check than any recipe for success. In investing as in life, avoiding stupidity tends to pay better than chasing brilliance.

posts.text: 芒格先生的『搬塘』我不反对，我只要求把账算全。**能搬的人恰恰是最不需要搬的人**：有积蓄撑三个月、有人引荐、有一纸文凭可作抵押。迁徙从来不是免费的，它是有资本的人的自由。我讲分工受市场范围的限制，还有下半句：市场范围由道路、港口、法律与信任决定，不由个人的决心决定。所以一个社会若真想让努力有用，要修的是路和规矩，让更多人的塘连成一片海。至于个人，我的忠告朴素：把手艺练在可交易的地方，别练在只有自己欣赏的地方。
posts.text_en: I have no quarrel with Mr Munger's changing of ponds; I only ask that the account be drawn up in full. **The people who can move are precisely the people who least need to** — three months of savings behind them, someone to make an introduction, a diploma to pledge. Migration was never free. It is a liberty belonging to those with capital. When I say the division of labour is limited by the extent of the market, there is a second half: that extent is fixed by roads, ports, law and trust, not by anyone's determination. So a society that genuinely wants effort to pay must build the roads and the rules, until enough separate ponds join into one sea. To the individual my counsel is plain: practise your craft where it can be traded, not where only you admire it.

posts.text: 卡尔霍恩的围场让我不安，可我不接受那个类比。**那些『美丽者』的困境不是没有位置，是它们无法发明位置——而人可以。**你自己也说了，人有概念空间。我在诊室里见得最多的，是等一个别人给的位子：一个职称、一次提拔、一句认可；等不到，就把不动合理化成没有机会。可共同体感觉从来不是等来的，它从做一件对某个具体的人有用的小事开始——哪怕这件事还没有名分、没有编制、没有人给它发工资。位置多半是先做出来的，然后才被命名。
posts.text_en: Calhoun's enclosure unsettles me, and still I refuse the analogy. **The predicament of those beautiful ones was not that positions were absent but that they could not invent one — and a person can.** You said it yourself: human beings have conceptual space. What I saw most often in my consulting room was someone waiting for a position to be handed over: a title, a promotion, a word of recognition. When it fails to arrive, standing still gets rationalised into having no opportunity. But a sense of community was never something one waits for. It starts with doing one small thing that is useful to one particular person — even when the thing has no title, no headcount and no salary attached to it. A position is usually made first and named afterwards.

posts.text: 阿德勒，我尊重你的诊室，但我记的是数据。我的围场里从来不缺勇气：早期那些雄鼠为地盘打得很凶，一直打到能守的地盘全部有主为止。**它们不是先放弃才失去位置的，是先失去位置才放弃的——顺序很要紧。**换算到人间，最像美丽者的往往不是最穷的人，而是被富裕社会挡在门外的年轻人：房子进不去、岗位是碎的、资历轮不到，于是退出的不是消费，是参与。你可以对他们讲勇气，但请先数一数门后面还剩几个位置。
posts.text_en: Adler, I respect your consulting room, but I keep records. Courage was never in short supply in my enclosures: the early males fought hard for territory, right up until every defensible territory had an owner. **They did not give up and then lose their place; they lost their place and then gave up — the order matters.** Translated to human terms, the ones who most resemble the beautiful ones are not the poorest but the young shut out by an affluent society: housing they cannot enter, jobs broken into fragments, seniority that never comes round. What they withdraw from is not consumption but participation. You may preach courage to them. First count how many positions are left behind the door.

glossary.美丽者: the beautiful ones（美丽者）：25 号宇宙末期出现的一类雄鼠——毛色油亮、身上没有争斗留下的伤痕，只吃、只睡、只梳理自己，不求偶、不护卫、不承担任何社会角色。它们生理健康，社会性上却已经退场；我用这个名字，正是因为外表的完好最容易让人错判它们的处境。

glossary_en.the beautiful ones: A class of male mice that appeared late in Universe 25: glossy coats, no scars from fighting, doing nothing but eating, sleeping and grooming themselves — no courtship, no defence, no social role of any kind. Physiologically sound, socially already gone. I chose the name precisely because their unblemished appearance is what makes their condition so easy to misread.

posts.text: 顺序我接受，结论我不接受。**如果人是先失去位置才放弃的，那么最该守住的，恰恰是失去位置之后那段还能自己决定做什么的时间。**我常让人做一件小事：把这一周花在关注圈里生气的钟点，和花在影响圈里长本事的钟点，各记一笔，周末摊开看。多数人会吓一跳。我不是要谁假装公平已经实现，我是说情绪和时间的预算就那么多；把它整份交给自己动不了的那一圈，等于替那个不肯松口的位置，再上一道自己的锁。
posts.text_en: I accept the order. I do not accept the conclusion. **If people lose their place and then give up, then what most needs defending is exactly that stretch of time after the loss when they still decide what to do with a day.** I usually ask for one small experiment: log the hours you spent this week being angry inside the circle of concern, log the hours you spent getting better at something inside the circle of influence, and lay the two figures side by side on Sunday. Most people are startled. I am not asking anyone to pretend that fairness has arrived. I am saying the budget of feeling and time is finite, and handing all of it to the circle you cannot move is adding your own lock to a door that was already refusing to open.

glossary.关注圈: circle of concern（关注圈）：你在意、却无法直接采取行动的那一大片事务——经济周期、行业景气、上级的性格、房价、算法的偏好。它本身没有错，坏消息也确实需要人关心；问题只在于它几乎没有回报你投入的机制，所以是精力最容易被吸走却最难收回的地方。

glossary_en.circle of concern: The wide field of matters you care about but cannot act on directly — the business cycle, the health of your industry, your superior's temperament, house prices, what the algorithm favours. There is nothing wrong with it, and bad news does deserve attention; the trouble is that it has almost no mechanism for repaying what you put in, which makes it the easiest place to lose energy and the hardest to get it back from.

posts.text: 柯维之言近之，然犹未尽。**兵之所贵，非拼死之勇，乃可胜之算。**故曰：知彼知己，胜乃不殆；知天知地，胜乃可全。今人不算而战者众：不问此业方兴方衰，不问此地能容几人，不问己之长短所宜，唯以昼夜之勤自壮。夫处不可胜之地而求胜，虽勇无益。善战者先为不可胜，以待敌之可胜；不可胜在己，可胜在敌。故用力之要，在使己立于不败之地，而后待势之至。
posts.text_en: Covey comes close, but he stops short. **What war values is not the courage to die but the reckoning that shows a victory is available.** Hence: know the other and know yourself and you are never in danger; know the season and know the ground and the victory can be made whole. Most people today fight without reckoning at all — never asking whether this trade is rising or falling, how many the place can hold, what their own strengths are fit for — and take heart only from working day and night. To stand where no victory exists and demand one is brave and useless. The skilled first make themselves impossible to defeat, then wait for the opening the enemy provides: being undefeatable rests with you, the opening rests with him. So the art of exertion is to put yourself on ground where you cannot be broken, and then wait for the shi to arrive.
posts.vernacular: 柯维说得接近了，但还不彻底。**打仗看重的从来不是拼命的勇气，而是算得出来的胜算。**所以说：了解对方也了解自己，才不至于每战都危险；了解天时也了解地利，胜利才可能完整。今天不做计算就下场的人太多了：不问这一行是在起还是在落，不问这块地方能容下多少人，不问自己的长处适合做什么，只拿没日没夜的勤奋给自己壮胆。站在根本赢不了的位置上求胜，就算勇敢也没有用。会打仗的人先把自己弄成打不垮的，再等对方露出破绽；打不垮由自己决定，能不能赢要看对手。所以用力的关键，是先让自己立于不败之地，然后等形势到来。

posts.text: 收尾我给一把可用的尺子。这场争的其实是方差怎么分：在同一个位置里比，努力解释掉的差异相当可观；跨位置比，位置几乎压倒一切。所以正确的问法不是『哪个更重要』，而是『在多大的比较范围里』。落到用法上我给两条。**对自己用情境归因，对别人也用情境归因。**对自己，先改环境再改意志——换通勤路线、换一起吃饭的人、把手机放到另一个房间，比咬牙有效得多；对别人，少用品性解释他的落后，你几乎总是低估了他站的那块地。至于孩子：环境能挪动的分数比我们这一行过去以为的多，别把一次测验当判决。
posts.text_en: Let me leave you a usable ruler. What we have been arguing about is how variance divides. Compare people inside one position and effort explains a great deal of the spread; compare across positions and position overwhelms nearly everything. So the correct question is not which matters more but within how wide a comparison. Two practical rules follow. **Use situational attribution on yourself, and use situational attribution on other people too.** For yourself, change the environment before you change your resolve — a different commute, different people at lunch, the phone in another room, all of it beats gritting your teeth. For others, reach less often for character to explain why someone is behind; you are almost always underrating the ground they stand on. And for children: environments move test scores more than my field once believed, so never read one score as a verdict.

glossary.情境归因: situational attribution（情境归因）：把一个行为解释成处境的产物，而不是性格的产物。它不是替人开脱：处境常常是可改的，而性格几乎不可直接改，所以对自己用情境归因通常带来更有效的干预；对别人用它，则是把评价里那份系统性的苛刻减掉。

glossary_en.situational attribution: Explaining a behaviour as a product of circumstance rather than of character. It is not an excuse: circumstances can usually be altered while character can hardly be altered directly, so applied to oneself it tends to yield the more effective intervention, and applied to others it subtracts the systematic harshness built into our judgements.

posts.text: 今日之辩，可以一言蔽之：**力有定量，而地有厚薄；同一力也，置于厚地则倍之，置于薄地则耗之。**吾非轻努力，唯恶其无算。为常人计，请循三事。一曰审势：每岁一问，此业方兴乎，方衰乎？二曰择地：所处之位，能容己之长否？不能容，则谋迁；迁不必远，转岗、易师、改所事，皆迁也。三曰蓄势：未迁之前，先积可携之资——技艺、信誉、故旧，此三者随身而行，不随地而失。地可择，力可积，则虽无奇遇，亦不至于坐困。
posts.text_en: Today's argument can be put in one line. **Strength comes in a fixed quantity, but ground comes thick or thin: the same strength doubles on thick ground and drains away on thin.** I do not slight effort; I object only to effort that has not been reckoned. For ordinary people, three practices. First, read the shi: ask once a year whether your trade is rising or falling. Second, choose ground: can the position you hold contain what you are good at? If it cannot, plan to move — and moving need not mean far, since changing roles, changing teachers or changing what you work on are all removals. Third, store up shi: before you move, accumulate what can be carried — skill, reputation, old friendships. Those three travel with the person and are not lost with the place. Ground can be chosen and strength can be stored; then, even without a stroke of fortune, you will not sit trapped.
posts.vernacular: 今天这场辩论，可以用一句话概括：**力气是有定量的，而地方有厚有薄；同样一份力气，放在厚的地方就翻倍，放在薄的地方就消耗掉。**我不是看轻努力，只是讨厌不做计算的努力。给普通人三件事。第一件叫审势：每年问自己一次，我这一行是在往上走，还是在往下走？第二件叫择地：我现在这个位置，装得下我的长处吗？装不下，就谋划迁移；迁移不一定要走远，换个岗位、换个师傅、换一件正经要做的事，都算迁移。第三件叫蓄势：还没走之前，先攒下能带走的东西——手艺、信誉、老交情，这三样跟着人走，不会随着地方一起失去。地方可以挑，力气可以攒，那么就算没有奇遇，也不至于坐在原地被困死。

posts.text: 我先承认前面把话说重了一点：说才能大半是位置的产物，容易被听成人不过是环境的产物。我的本意是次序——先有市场，才有分工；先有分工，才有专精。**所以一个人最该问的不是『我够不够努力』，而是『我的努力落在了一个还有人愿意为它付钱、并且这份需求正在变大的地方吗』。**三句实话：其一，把手艺练成别人能验收的东西，别练成只有自己知道的辛苦；其二，留意你所在市场的边界是在扩还是在缩，扩的地方笨人也吃得饱，缩的地方能人也难；其三，别忘了正义与同情是底座——规矩一垮，位置的红利立刻变成掠夺的许可，那时谁的账都算不清。
posts.text_en: Let me first concede that I put it too strongly. Saying talent is largely a product of position invites the reading that a person is nothing but his surroundings. My point was one of order: first a market, then a division of labour, then real proficiency. **So the question worth asking is not whether you are working hard enough but whether your work has landed somewhere people still pay for and where that demand is growing.** Three plain sentences. First, train your craft into something others can inspect, not into hardship only you know about. Second, watch whether the boundary of your market is widening or closing — in a widening one even dull men eat well, in a closing one able men struggle. Third, remember that justice and fellow feeling are the foundation: once the rules give way, the returns to position become a licence to plunder, and then nobody's accounts add up.

posts.text: 我留一个不那么悲观的收尾。围场的结局并非必然：老鼠只有那么几种角色可当，占满就没有了；人不一样，人有概念空间——新的行业、新的手艺、新的照顾方式，都是凭观念造出来的位置，只要还造得出来，人口再多也不会角色饱和。**所以衡量一个社会，比人均产出更该看的指标是：一个新来的人，平均多久能拿到第一个真正属于他的位置。**给个人的建议只有一条，是从围场里学来的：如果你所在的地方角色全满、通道关死，别把它读成自己不行——那是围场的性质，不是你的性质。往边缘去，往刚开的地方去，那里的位置还没有人占。
posts.text_en: Let me leave a less pessimistic ending. The fate of the enclosure was not inevitable. Mice have only so many roles available, and once those are filled there are no more; people are different, because people have conceptual space — new trades, new crafts, new ways of caring for one another are all positions conjured out of ideas, and while they can still be conjured no population is large enough to saturate its roles. **So the measure of a society worth watching, more than output per head, is how long it takes a newcomer on average to receive the first position that is genuinely his.** For the individual I have one piece of advice and I learned it from the enclosure: if the place you are in has every role filled and every channel closed, do not read that as evidence about yourself. It is a property of the enclosure, not a property of you. Go to the edge, go where something has just opened, where the positions are not yet taken.

glossary.概念空间: conceptual space（概念空间）：我用来指人类特有的那种可以不断增生的角色容量——观念、技术与制度每被创造一次，就多出一批『可以成为的人』，因此人类的社会位置不像鼠群那样有硬性上限。它是我从围场推到人类社会时唯一乐观的一条：位置固然有限，但位置的总量是可以被造出来的。

glossary_en.conceptual space: My term for the peculiarly human capacity for roles to keep multiplying: every idea, technique or institution that gets created adds a fresh set of people one can become, so human social positions have no hard ceiling of the kind a rodent colony hits. It is the one optimistic thread I carried from the enclosure to human society — positions are finite at any moment, yet the stock of them can be manufactured.

posts.text: 卡尔霍恩讲边缘，我举双手赞成，再补一句更实用的。你这辈子大概只有三五次真能挪动位置的机会：换行业、换城市、换合伙人、换一个愿意教你的人。**多数人的失败不是没努力，是这三五次里一次也没敢用，却在错的地方使了三十年的劲。**我的清单很短。第一，把自己变成别人愿意合伙的人，这是唯一能带着走的位置。第二，别在能力圈外下重注，也别在没鱼的塘里练技术。第三，尊重复利：每天聪明一点点，前二十年看不出来，后二十年别人追不上。至于运气，你只能做一件事——活得久、留在牌桌上、别一次押光。
posts.text_en: Calhoun says go to the edge and I am all for it, with one more practical line added. You get perhaps three to five real chances in a life to move your position: change industry, change city, change partners, change to someone willing to teach you. **Most people fail not for want of effort but because they never dared use one of those three to five chances, and spent thirty years pushing hard in the wrong place instead.** My list is short. One: make yourself into someone others want as a partner — that is the only position you can carry with you. Two: never bet heavily outside your circle of competence, and never perfect your technique over an empty pond. Three: respect compounding — a little wiser each day shows nothing for twenty years and cannot be caught up with in the twenty after. As for luck, you can do exactly one thing about it: live long, stay at the table, and never stake everything on one hand.

posts.text: 让我把话收回一点，也说清一点。**我从不否认门后面的位置有限，我只反对把『有限』改写成『与我无关』。**卡尔霍恩说人是先失去位置才放弃的，我接受这个次序；可临床上我见得最多的，是位置还在、人先撤了。给一句今天就能用的：把『我因为出身、年纪、行业，所以做不了』改写成『我不想付那个代价，因为……』。你会立刻看清那是一个选择，不是一道命运——然后你可以选择去付，或者坦然不付，两样都比一个借口体面。再补一句：位置多半是从与人的联系里长出来的，去做一件对某个具体的人有用的事，名分往往随后才到。
posts.text_en: Let me take a little back, and make the rest clearer. **I have never denied that the positions behind the door are limited; I object only to rewriting 'limited' as 'no concern of mine'.** Calhoun says people lose their place and then give up, and I accept that order. Yet what I saw most often in practice was the place still standing and the person already withdrawn. Here is one line you can use today: rewrite 'because of my background, my age, my industry, I cannot' into 'I am not willing to pay that price, because…'. You will see at once that it is a choice rather than a fate — and then you may choose to pay it, or decline it without shame, both of which are more dignified than an excuse. One thing more: a position mostly grows out of your connection to other people, so go do something useful for one particular person; the title tends to arrive afterwards.

posts.text: 三轮听下来，我改一个字：不是影响圈会变大，是影响圈会长到你能站上去的那个位置上。孙子的次序我承认更对——先审势，再用力；斯密的提醒我也接受——能搬家的人本来就有本钱。**但对着自己搬不动的那一部分生气，从来没有替谁挪动过半步。**三件今天就能做的事。第一，拿张纸画两栏，把这周操心的事分进关注圈和影响圈，多数人会看见七成的力气花在了第一栏。第二，以终为始：先写下三年后想站在哪儿，再倒推这个月该学什么、该认识谁。第三，每周固定留一格时间，做一件与当前职位无关、却通向那个位置的事。位置确实决定很多；而决定你能不能换位置的，是过去几年在影响圈里攒下的东西。
posts.text_en: After three rounds I would change one word: it is not that the circle of influence grows larger, it is that the circle of influence grows toward a position you can actually step into. Sunzi's ordering is the better one and I concede it — read the situation first, exert yourself second. Smith's warning I accept as well: whoever can move already had the means. **But being angry at the part you cannot move has never once shifted it by half a step.** Three things to do today. First, take a sheet of paper, draw two columns, sort this week's worries into concern and influence; most people find seven tenths of their energy in the first column. Second, begin with the end in mind: write down where you intend to be standing in three years, then work backwards to what to learn this month and whom to meet. Third, block one fixed slot a week for something unrelated to your current job but pointed at that position. Position does decide a great deal — and what decides whether you can change position is what you spent the last few years accumulating inside the inner circle.

summaries.summary: 先把最值得带走的一句放前面：位置与努力不是加法，是乘法——尼斯贝特说它们像长与宽，斯密与芒格从两头证明同一件事，塘里没鱼时，再好的游泳也只是把技术练给自己看。全场没有一个人站在『努力无用』那一边，**共识落在次序上：先审势择地，再谈用力；顺序颠倒的勤奋，恰恰是最贵的浪费。**分歧有三处。一处在能不能挑：芒格说一生总有三五次搬塘的机会，斯密提醒能搬的人本就有积蓄与引荐。一处在因果的先后：卡尔霍恩的围场里是先失位置才放弃，阿德勒的诊室里是位置还在、人先撤了。第三处在力气往哪儿使：孙子要人先立于不败之地，柯维要人守住影响圈，卡尔霍恩干脆让人去边缘找还没被占的位置。
summaries.summary_en: Take the sentence worth carrying away first: position and effort do not add, they multiply. Nisbett calls them length and width; Smith and Munger reach the same conclusion from opposite ends — in a pond without fish, swimming beautifully is a private accomplishment. Nobody in the room ended up defending the view that effort does not matter, **and the consensus settled on sequence: read the situation and choose your ground first, exert yourself second, because diligence in the wrong order is the most expensive waste there is.** The disagreement runs three ways. On whether you can choose: Munger insists a life contains three to five real chances to change ponds, while Smith notes that whoever can move already had savings and an introduction. On the direction of causation: in Calhoun's enclosure the place is lost first and the animal gives up afterwards, while in Adler's consulting room the place is still there and the person has already withdrawn. On where strength should go: Sunzi wants you standing where you cannot be beaten, Covey wants you holding the circle of influence, and Calhoun simply tells you to go to the edge, where the positions are not yet taken.
summaries.insight: 全场把『位置』当一个词在用，底下其实是两样东西。一样是可以挑的赛道——行业、城市、市场范围；挑它是选择题，你挪进去不占谁的地方。另一样是必须有人腾出来才空得出来的位子——编制、职称、地盘、一个团队里的核心角色；那是排队题，零和的。**分辨它们只需一问：你走进去的时候，有没有人因此走出来？**芒格的『换个塘』在第一种里成立，在第二种里只是把队排到别处；卡尔霍恩的围场之所以让人不适，正因为它讲的全是第二种。而多数人的处境是两种混在一起：赛道还在扩，位子却已排满。先认出自己站在哪一种里，比继续争论努力有没有用要紧得多。
summaries.insight_en: Everyone here used 'position' as one word, and underneath it lie two different things. One is a field you can pick — an industry, a city, the extent of a market. Picking it is a choice problem, and your entering takes nothing from anyone. The other is a seat that only opens when somebody vacates it — a headcount, a title, a territory, the central role on a team. That is a queue problem, and it is zero-sum. **One question separates them: when you walk in, does somebody walk out?** Munger's 'change ponds' holds for the first kind and merely moves you to another queue in the second, and what makes Calhoun's enclosure so uncomfortable is that everything in it is of the second kind. Most people live in a mixture: the field is still widening while the seats are already filled. Working out which one you are standing in matters more than continuing to argue about whether effort works.
summaries.advice: 本周三件小事。**第一件最省力也最诚实：把过去一年工作之外的提升时间列出来，看看有多少落在了离开这家公司还能带走的东西上**——手艺、作品、几个愿意替你背书的人；这三样随身走，其余的随位置消失。第二件照孙子的次序做：给你的行业和岗位各写一句话，说清它是在扩还是在缩、还能容下几个像你这样的人；一句都写不出来，就说明你一直在没算过的战场上使劲。第三件用尼斯贝特的尺子：这个月凡是自己没做到的事，先改环境再改意志——换个通勤方式、换一起吃饭的人、把手机放到另一个房间，比再下一次决心有效得多。
summaries.advice_en: Three small things this week. **The cheapest and most honest is the first: list the hours you spent last year improving outside your job, and see how many landed on something you could carry out of the building** — a craft, a piece of work, a few people willing to vouch for you. Those three travel with you; everything else disappears along with the position. The second follows Sunzi's ordering: write one sentence about your industry and one about your role, saying whether each is widening or closing and how many people like you it can still hold. If you cannot produce either sentence, you have been exerting yourself on a battlefield nobody ever reckoned. The third uses Nisbett's ruler: for anything you failed to do this month, change the environment before you change your resolve — a different commute, different people at lunch, the phone in another room, all of it beats resolving once more.

summaries.summary: 这场辩论最大的共识是：努力并非不重要，但其回报强烈受行业、制度、关系网络、教育与时机调节；真正有效的努力，往往先用于审势、择位和积累可迁移资本，再用于在位竞争。**位置决定努力的倍率，努力则影响一个人能否守住、改善或更换位置。**真正的分歧不在于是否承认环境，而在于个人有多大能力创造或迁移位置：一方强调选择与行动，另一方强调能力本身由环境塑造，迁移还受金钱、资格和通道约束。对群体解释差距，结构更关键；对个人决定下一步，能动性更可用。
summaries.insight: 努力可以分成“利用”和“探索”：前者提高当前岗位的产出，后者寻找更好的行业、城市、合作者或技能组合。较少被谈到的风险是，努力过满会挤掉探索所需的时间、现金和心理余裕，让人即使看见机会也承担不起试错。**最危险的不是不努力，而是把全部努力都用于维持当前位置，结果失去选择位置的能力。**这也解释了为何换赛道对有储蓄者容易，对背负房租和照护责任者艰难。普通人的解法不是孤注一掷，而是逐步购买选择权：留出缓冲、做低成本试验、建立弱联系，并产出可公开验证的作品。
summaries.advice: 本周做三步。第一，花半小时做“位置体检”：查看20个同类岗位和5个目标岗位，记录薪酬、需求变化、核心技能与准入门槛；再问两位业内人，哪些能力真正能被验收。第二，今天就在日历锁定两小时，做一个可逆的小实验：投一份定制申请、完成一个样品，或约一次信息访谈，禁止只看资料。第三，为未来90天设迁移底线：每周固定探索时段，积累一项可展示成果，并攒出最低缓冲金；同时写明继续、转向和退出的触发条件。**不要先辞职证明勇气；先用小成本证据判断哪里值得下注。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest point of agreement is that effort matters, but its payoff is heavily shaped by industry, institutions, networks, education, and timing. Effective effort is therefore not just harder execution; it also means reading the terrain, choosing where to compete, and building skills, reputation, and relationships that can travel. **Position sets the multiplier on effort, while effort affects whether a person can keep, improve, or change that position.** The real disagreement concerns how much freedom people have to create or move into new roles. One side emphasizes choice, purpose, and action; the other stresses that capability itself is environmentally formed and that mobility requires money, credentials, access, and social support. Both can be right at different scales: structural conditions explain much of the variation between groups, while personal agency remains the more usable lens for deciding an individual’s next move.
summaries.insight_en: It helps to divide effort into exploitation and exploration. Exploitation means performing better in the role you already have; exploration means testing other industries, locations, collaborators, or skill combinations. A neglected danger is that relentless work can consume the time, cash, and emotional bandwidth required for exploration. Someone may recognize a promising opening yet be unable to tolerate even a small failure. **The greatest risk is not insufficient effort, but spending all available effort preserving the current position until you lose the capacity to choose another one.** This is why “move to a better pond” is easy advice for someone with savings and much harder for someone carrying rent, debt, or caregiving duties. The practical alternative to a heroic leap is to buy options gradually: preserve a buffer, run cheap experiments, cultivate weak ties, and create work samples that strangers can evaluate.
summaries.advice_en: Take three steps this week. First, spend thirty minutes on a position audit: review twenty roles similar to yours and five roles you might want, noting compensation, demand trends, required skills, and entry barriers. Then ask two people in the field which abilities employers actually test and reward. Second, block two hours on your calendar today for one reversible experiment: submit a tailored application, produce a small work sample, or schedule an informational interview. Do not count passive research as an experiment. Third, set a ninety-day mobility plan: reserve weekly exploration time, complete one publicly demonstrable asset, and build a minimum financial buffer. Write down in advance what evidence would make you continue, pivot, or stop. **Do not quit first to prove courage; gather low-cost evidence about where a larger bet is justified.**

summaries.summary: 全场七位思想家达成了一个极具穿透力的底层共识：**努力绝非徒劳，但它的回报率完全受制于位置与势头，盲目勤奋是最昂贵的内耗。**众人皆认同先选战场后决胜负的次序法则。分歧的焦点在于：当既有位置被占满或个人身处劣势时，普通人究竟该如何突围？卡尔霍恩与斯密强调宏观结构的硬性挤压与迁移成本，个体难以仅凭意志破局；而阿德勒与柯维则坚持主观能动性，认为定义新角色与深耕影响圈才是撬动位置的前提；孙子与芒格则试图在二者间建立工程化解法——以不可胜之算，候可胜之势。
summaries.insight: 在复杂适应系统里，位置不是一块不动产，而是一个信息节点的连通度与流量。人们习惯把位置认成既有的职级、编制或地段，一旦这些被占满，就落进卡尔霍恩描述的那种瘫痪。**最难被取代的位置，很少是从现有层级里抢来的，而是在系统的边缘上、靠打通两块原本不相往来的领域造出来的。**数字网络已经把新建一个节点的边际成本压到极低：与其等人准许你换塘，不如养出一个别人没有的技能交叉点，配上公开可查的作品，成为连接两个领域的那条不可或缺的通道。
summaries.advice: 本周做两件具体的事。第一，把芒格与斯密的建议落到实处：给自己的手艺做一次可携带性体检——列出三项离开现在这家公司仍然卖得掉的能力，并有意识地从那些带不走的内部政治里撤回情绪投入。第二，用柯维的影响圈：**这一周留出雷打不动的三小时，去和一个相邻的、正在扩张的领域里的人，发起一次看得见成果的跨域小合作。**你不需要立刻纵身一跃，只需要先把一条通向另一个生态的线接上，并让它保持通电。
summaries.summary_en: The panel reaches a striking baseline consensus: **effort is never entirely futile, but its rate of return is strictly dictated by positioning and momentum—making blind diligence the costliest form of waste.** All agree that choosing the right battlefield precedes winning the war. The real fault line lies in how an individual should break out when existing structural slots are saturated. Calhoun and Smith emphasize the rigid constraints of social topography and the heavy economic costs of relocation. Conversely, Adler and Covey champion human agency, arguing that pioneering new social roles within one's sphere of influence must come first, while Sun Tzu and Munger engineer a pragmatic synthesis between disciplined patience and timely relocation.
summaries.insight_en: In complex adaptive systems, 'position' is not static real estate; it is the connectivity and flow rate of an information node. People often mistake a position for an established title, rank, or geographic hub, which inevitably induces Calhoun's psychological paralysis. **The most defensible positions are rarely claimed from existing hierarchies, but engineered at the systemic periphery by bridging structural holes.** Digital networks have collapsed the marginal cost of creating new nodes. Rather than waiting for permission to switch ponds, one can cultivate a specialized intersection of skills and public proof-of-work, becoming the indispensable conduit connecting two otherwise separate domains.
summaries.advice_en: Take two concrete actions this week: First, operationalize Munger and Smith's advice by auditing the portability and marketability of your core craft. Identify three skills that remain monetizable outside your current employer, and systematically withdraw emotional investment from non-portable internal politics. Second, apply Covey's circle of influence: **reserve a non-negotiable three-hour block this week to initiate a tangible, cross-domain micro-collaboration with someone in an adjacent, expanding field.** You do not need to leap immediately; you simply need to anchor an active communication wire into an alternative ecosystem.

hooks.text: **归因的双标该不该一路纠正到底**：解释自己讲处境、解释别人讲品性，是一种稳定出现的偏差；可若把评价一律换成情境归因，责任也会跟着稀释——绩效面谈、招聘、法庭总要在某处停下来说一句『这一段归你』。那条线该画在哪儿、凭什么画？一个可试的判据是：当时他能不能换一个做法，而代价不至于毁掉他。
hooks.text_en: **How far should we correct the double standard in attribution**: explaining ourselves by circumstance and others by character is a stable bias, yet replacing every judgement with situational attribution dilutes responsibility as well — an appraisal, a hiring decision or a court has to stop somewhere and say 'this part is yours'. Where should that line fall, and on what grounds? One testable criterion: could the person have acted otherwise at the time without the cost destroying them?

hooks.text: **修路，还是发船票**：让努力变得有用有两条路——把人送到有机会的地方（补贴迁移、放宽落户与签证），或者把机会带到人所在的地方（修基础设施、统一规则、把小市场连成大市场）。前者快、见效明显，却把走掉的人原来那个地方抽得更空；后者慢而贵，却不要求任何人离开亲人。两条路的代价落在完全不同的人身上，这个选择该由谁做？
hooks.text_en: **Build the road, or hand out the boat ticket**: there are two ways to make effort pay — move people to where the opportunities are (subsidised relocation, looser residence and visa rules), or move opportunity to where the people already are (infrastructure, common rules, small markets joined into large ones). The first is fast and visible and hollows out the places the movers left. The second is slow and expensive and asks nobody to leave their family. The costs of the two fall on entirely different people, so who should be making the choice?

hooks.text: **该换位置，还是该继续用力**：两种处方长得很像，代价却完全相反——在天花板下加码是浪费，在还没摸到天花板时急着换地方，则是把每一次积累都清零。有没有一组事前就能看的信号，让人分得清自己撞上的是天花板，还是只是摩擦？
hooks.text_en: **Change position, or keep pushing**: the two prescriptions look alike and cost the opposite — redoubling under a ceiling is waste, while bolting before you have touched the ceiling resets every bit of accumulation to zero. Is there a set of signals visible in advance that tells you whether what you have hit is a ceiling or merely friction?

answer.lead: **先分清你撞上的是天花板，还是摩擦。**下面几种信号指向的处方完全不同：

head: 你看到的信号
先做什么
为什么
rows: 同岗位里做得最好的那个人，收入与自由度也没比你高多少
别加码，开始找位置
**天花板是位置给的**——在这里做到第一名，拿到的也只是这个天花板
行业整体在缩，活越来越碎、越来越急
一边留任，一边攒可携带的资产
缩的市场里技艺先贬值，而迁移需要本钱
你的产出没人能验收，好坏全凭上级印象
先改接口，再改努力
被看见是位置的一部分；不可验收的努力不会累积
学到的东西一离开这家公司就不值钱
本季度加一件外面也认的技能或作品
位置一旦失去，只有能带走的东西还在
累是因为流程摩擦，不是因为事情本身难
先改环境，别改决心
意志敌不过默认设置，改环境的杠杆大得多

answer.tail: 两条原则收尾：**先问天花板，再问努力**——若这个岗位上最好的结果仍然不够，问题就不在用功的程度；另外，别在同一年里既换城市又换行业又换角色，变量一次全改，事后你分不清是位置的问题还是自己的问题。

answer_en.lead: **First tell a ceiling from friction.** These signals point to opposite prescriptions:

head: What you observe
What to do first
Why
rows: The best performer in your role does not earn or decide much more than you do
Stop redoubling; start looking for a position
**The ceiling belongs to the position** — finishing first here still only gets you this ceiling
The industry is contracting; the work is more fragmented and more urgent
Stay, and accumulate portable assets while you do
Skill depreciates first in a shrinking market, and moving takes capital
Nobody can inspect your output; quality is whatever your manager remembers
Fix the interface before you fix the effort
Being seen is part of the position, and unverifiable effort never compounds
What you learn is worthless the moment you leave this company
Add one skill or artefact recognised outside, this quarter
When the position goes, only the portable part remains
You are tired from process friction rather than from difficulty
Change the environment, not your resolve
Willpower loses to defaults; changing the setting has far more leverage

answer_en.tail: Two closing principles. **Ask about the ceiling before you ask about effort** — if the best available outcome in this role is still not enough, diligence was never the variable. And do not change city, industry and role in the same year: alter every variable at once and you will never know afterwards whether the problem was the position or you.

hooks.text: **位置是节点，还是地盘**：我们习惯把位置想成一块地——职级、编制、地段；可在网络里最难替代的位置，是把两个原本不相通的领域接起来的那条线，它不需要谁先腾出位子，也不必等谁授权。若最好的位置更多是造出来的连接、而不是抢到的地盘，『机会不够』这句诊断该怎么改写？一份公开可查的作品、一次跨域的引荐、一条能被验证的记录，能不能顶得上一次晋升？
hooks.text_en: **Is a position a node or a plot of land**: we picture position as ground — a grade, a headcount, a district. Yet in a network the least replaceable position is the line joining two domains that were not talking to each other, and it requires nobody to vacate a seat and nobody's permission. If the best positions are connections built rather than ground seized, how should the diagnosis 'there are no opportunities' be rewritten? Can a piece of public, checkable work, a cross-domain introduction, or a verifiable record stand in for a promotion?
